title: Responsive images: should we define source selection normatively instead of leaving it implementation-defined
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

All three engines implement the same rule:
- sort by density
- pick the first candidate whose density ≥ the device pixel ratio (including page zoom)
-  if none, pick the last.

There is one blink-related optimization to prefer an already-loaded higher-density candidate, but it's an interop issue and rarely used.

The implementation-defined facade is costly:
- It's untestable. WPT can only test de-duplication ([select-an-image-source.html](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/html/semantics/embedded-content/the-img-element/srcset/select-an-image-source.html)); nothing can assert currentSrc for w/x selection. The behaviour is universal but unenforced.
- Authors already rely on the exact rule. Every workaround in #13069 (inflated w descriptors, sizes lies, optimumx-style libraries) only works because "first ≥ DPR" is universal. The spec says they can't depend on it; the ecosystem does.
- New work needs a defined baseline. #13069 proposes a multiplier/priority on the selected density; naturalWidth-from-density (#13046, #12565) exposes the choice to script; the sizes=auto reselection loop (#12248) needs a known selection function to reason about stability. A multiplier on an undefined choice is undefined.
 
Proposing to cement the existing behavior. If UAs want to do something different in the future, we can review whether implementation-defined behavior would be web compatible.

Note CSS is in the same state — css-images-4 says image-set() lets "the UA decide which is most appropriate". Blink unified the two in 2024; defining one gives the CSSWG something to reference.
